hook: Lemon Squeezy is closed to new stores and will stop processing on March 31, 2027. In the same $20 subscription model, Stripe Payments + Billing with no-code Tax costs $1,120, with Tax API $1,520, Paddle $1,500, and legacy Lemon Squeezy $1,600.

sections.title: Lemon Squeezy is winding down: what existing stores need to do
sections.content:
Lemon Squeezy closed new-user and store sign-ups on November 16, 2026. Tools for eligible stores are planned for December 2; start by mid-January 2027. Processing and renewals stop March 31, 2027, with no extensions.

Its fee examples here are a legacy baseline. See the [migration guide](https://docs.lemonsqueezy.com/migration) for the official dates.

| Stripe component | Published rate | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic cards | 2.9% + 30¢ | successful charge |
| International cards | +1.5% | applicable international cards |
| Currency conversion | +1% | when conversion is required |
| Billing pay-as-you-go | 0.7% | Billing volume |
| Tax Basic no-code | 0.5% | registered transactions |
| Tax Basic API | 50¢ | registered transactions |

Use one Tax Basic path, not both. These are US rates; registration and filing are separate.

sections.title: Paddle and legacy Lemon Squeezy have different fee rules
sections.content:
Paddle and the legacy Lemon Squeezy rate card list a base 5% + 50¢, but their subscription invoices differ.

- Lemon Squeezy adds 0.5 percentage points for subscriptions, 1.5 for applicable non-US transactions and 1.5 for PayPal. Its fee uses the total order value, including tax.
- Paddle advertises 5% + 50¢ per Checkout transaction with subscriptions included. Do not copy Lemon Squeezy surcharges onto Paddle.
- Account-specific pricing, payouts and optional services can change either result.

A merchant of record handles covered transaction tax obligations as the seller. That is not a promise that your business has no income-tax, reporting or other legal obligations. Compare the service scope as well as the checkout fee.

sections.title: Four invoices for the same subscription volume
sections.content:
Assume 1,000 US domestic card renewals at $20 each. Every charge incurs the chosen Tax Basic fee. Excludes added tax, refunds, disputes, FX, payouts and Lemon Squeezy international or PayPal fees.

| Provider / path | Arithmetic | Total |
|---|---|---|
| Stripe + no-code Tax | $580 + $300 Payments + $140 Billing + $100 Tax | $1,120 |
| Stripe + Tax API | $580 + $300 + $140 + $500 | $1,520 |
| Legacy Lemon Squeezy subscription | 5.5% × $20,000 + 1,000 × $0.50 | $1,600 |
| Paddle standard | 5% × $20,000 + 1,000 × $0.50 | $1,500 |

Correction, November 14: the earlier $1,500 Lemon Squeezy subscription example omitted its surcharge. The old universal $21.43 crossover also assumed the Tax API path and Paddle's base rate, not every subscription setup.

sections.title: Country and tax change the denominator
sections.content:
Use the actual checkout total, not just the advertised product price. A hypothetical $20 subscription with 20% tax creates a $24 order; if Lemon Squeezy's non-US surcharge applies, its fee is 7% × $24 + $0.50 = $2.18, before payout costs.

| Change from the base model | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Lemon Squeezy non-US subscription | 7% + 50¢; PayPal can add another 1.5 points |
| Stripe international card | add 1.5 points to its applicable stack |
| Stripe FX conversion | add 1 point when required |
| Tax-inclusive versus tax-exclusive price | calculate from the actual fee base |

Payout fees are separate and excluded from the totals.

sections.title: The crossover belongs to one set of assumptions
sections.content:
With the same tax-free US model, Stripe plus no-code Tax is 4.1% × P + $0.30 per charge, lower than both modeled MoR fees at every positive P. With Tax API it is 3.6% × P + $0.80.

- Against Paddle: $0.30 / (5% − 3.6%) = $21.43.
- Against a Lemon Squeezy subscription: $0.30 / (5.5% − 3.6%) = $15.79.
- A $9 Lemon Squeezy subscription costs $0.995 before other fees, not the $0.95 base one-time illustration.

Those are processing comparisons, not total operating costs. Neither result prices engineering, tax registration, filing, buyer support or risk. A cheaper fee model can still be the more expensive business process.

sections.title: Choose the service before trusting the headline
sections.content:
On Stripe Payments + Billing, you remain the seller. Tax Basic calculates and collects tax; separate Tax Complete plans cover filing and registration.

Stripe Managed Payments is a distinct merchant-of-record product outside this fee model. Stripe reviews account and product eligibility; its [business-location list](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/eligibility) does not include South Korea. Buyer coverage is separate.

Paddle acts as merchant of record for covered sales, as Lemon Squeezy does for existing stores until processing ends. Confirm approval, fees, payout timing, refunds and chargebacks, then test representative receipts and renewals before committing.

decision_matrix.pick: Plan the move before renewals stop
decision_matrix.why: Dec 2 tooling is planned for eligible stores only. Start by mid-January and replace links and any unsupported payment or fulfillment flows before March 31, 2027.

decision_matrix.situation: US domestic subscriptions with Checkout Tax
decision_matrix.why: The 0.5% path produces $1,120 here, not the $1,520 Tax API total.

decision_matrix.pick: Compare the viable paths and your legacy baseline
decision_matrix.why: At $20, Stripe Tax API is $1,520 and Paddle $1,500 under the base assumptions. Existing Lemon Squeezy stores can use $1,600 as a legacy comparison.
Factor in the actual surcharge and payout terms; use the Lemon Squeezy rates only to model existing transactions.
Covered tax handling can justify a higher fee, but business reporting and eligibility still require review.
The fixed 50¢ component weighs heavily; custom rates must be confirmed, not assumed.
South Korea is not on Stripe’s published Managed Payments business-location list. Buyer coverage and merchant onboarding are distinct; compare settlement for providers available to your business.

verdict_summary: Lemon Squeezy is closed to new stores and stops renewals on March 31, 2027. Existing stores should migrate before then. In the defined US $20 model, Stripe Payments + Billing with no-code Tax costs $1,120, with Tax API $1,520, Paddle $1,500, and legacy Lemon Squeezy $1,600. These are not Managed Payments prices.
migration_guide: Start by mid-January 2027. Export customer, order and subscription records; confirm eligible payment data and consent with both providers; test renewals, receipts and settlement before cutting over. Managed Payments cannot migrate PayPal-funded subscriptions and has no built-in storefront, digital delivery or affiliate tools. Arrange replacements and replace checkout links, embeds and integrations: old links do not redirect automatically. Move to another provider if the business or required features are ineligible.

faqs.q: Can a new business choose Lemon Squeezy now?
faqs.a: No. New users and stores closed November 16, 2026. Lemon Squeezy stops payment processing, including renewals, on March 31, 2027; its fees here are a comparison for existing stores.

faqs.q: Does an existing store automatically move to Stripe Managed Payments?
faqs.a: No. Lemon Squeezy plans tools for eligible stores on December 2, 2026 and recommends starting by mid-January. PayPal-funded subscriptions cannot move to Managed Payments, and old checkout links do not redirect automatically. Check account and product eligibility and arrange separate storefront, delivery and affiliate tools as needed.

faqs.q: Does Stripe Tax always cost 50¢ per transaction?
faqs.a: No. The US Tax Basic page distinguishes 0.5% no-code integrations from a 50¢ API integration charge for applicable registered transactions. They are alternative paths, not two fees to add together.

faqs.q: Do these calculations prove Korean eligibility or remove all tax duties?
faqs.a: No. South Korea is not on Stripe’s published list of supported Managed Payments business locations. Buyer coverage is not seller eligibility. Verify onboarding, settlement and business tax obligations separately.
